title: What If Five Centuries of Fishing Stopped in One Day? Cod Did

scenes.text: What if a fishery that fed people for five centuries shut down in one day?
On July 2nd, 1992, Canada banned fishing for northern cod off Newfoundland.
Catches had peaked at 810,000 tons in 1968. By 1992, spawning cod were about one percent of their peak.
About 30,000 people lost their jobs, roughly 12 percent of the province's workforce.
Newfoundland's population fell by a record 10 percent over the next decade.
A limited commercial cod fishery only returned in 2024, thirty-two years later.
